root_idea.summary: The root centers on cutting off or separating something. From this developed the ideas of acquiring something as though taking a portion, and of sin as a blameworthy acquisition or consequence.
root_idea.development: The same orientation extends to cutting wool or fruit, dates and date refuse, completion as being cut off from what precedes, acquisition or earning, and the body as something bounded or formed. The fixed expression لَا جَرَمَ developed an emphatic sense of inevitability or certainty.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic nominal occurs in the fixed expression لَا جَرَمَ, which is the appropriate public citation form.

senses.definition: To cause, induce, or incite someone to do or undergo something.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ + subject, the construction may express causing or inducing an outcome, including inciting someone toward sin; translations such as “incite,” “cause,” and “prevent” reflect the context rather than separate lexical senses.

senses.definition: To commit a sin, crime, fault, or other punishable wrongdoing.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic Form IV verb describes blameworthy acquisition or commission of wrongdoing; its subject may be a person or group, and the context may render the act as committing crimes or sins.

senses.definition: Committing a sin or other punishable wrongdoing; criminal conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun corresponding to أَجْرَمَ, referring to the act or responsibility of committing wrongdoing.

senses.definition: Surely; indeed; inevitably it is the case that.
senses.usage_conditions: A fixed Quranic expression, commonly followed by أَنَّ and a clause. It emphatically presents a consequence as certain or unavoidable and is variously rendered “indeed,” “surely,” or “no doubt”; it is not simply the ordinary noun جُرْمٌ “sin.”

senses.definition: A sinner, criminal, or person who commits punishable wrongdoing.
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle is used substantivally and adjectivally, with inflected forms referring to individuals or groups characterized by such wrongdoing.

senses.definition: The unbelievers, as a designation for those who reject faith.
senses.usage_conditions: This specialized plural usage is explicitly reported as a Quranic designation in a cited Quran passage; it is a contextual designation within the broader sense of culpable wrongdoing, not a general synonym for every unbeliever in all contexts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or cut off; to shear wool and to cut fruit from palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be wool, a sheep's fleece, palm trees, or dates; the palm-harvesting use includes cutting off the fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To estimate by conjecture the quantity of fruit on palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized palm-cultivation usage, also associated with acquiring or taking an estimated quantity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gain, acquire, or earn; to bring about or occasion a result.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The earning construction may refer to seeking sustenance for one's family. In causative-result contexts, an action is said to earn or occasion a consequence, such as anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commit a sin, crime, fault, offence, or act of disobedience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may take the sin or crime as its object or express commission against a person or group. This is the Form I lexical branch, distinct from the Quranic Form IV citation form أَجْرَمَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat the dates that have fallen during palm harvesting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage refers to fallen dates remaining among the palm branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become great in bodily size.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted discussion contains a disputed reading between enlargement of the body and enlargement of sin; the bodily interpretation is represented here as the preferred lexical correction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become clear in colour.
To become clear in the voice.
To adhere or stick to someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested examples concern blood adhering to a person or tar adhering to a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut off vehemently or repeatedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an intensive Form II cutting usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go forth from a group or people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction جَرَّمْنَاهُمْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To complete the winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II temporal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For dates to reach the time when they are to be cut from the palm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Form IV intransitive agricultural construction, distinct from the Quranic transitive wrongdoing sense of أَجْرَمَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become complete, end, or pass away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a year, winter, or night becoming completed or ending; it can also describe the passage of a specified number of nights.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To accuse someone of a sin or crime that the person did not commit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction specifically conveys a false or unfounded accusation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To guard oneself against committing sin or crime.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive ethical usage comparable to guarding oneself from sin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To call, cry out, shout, or vociferate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is associated with جِرْمٌ in the sense of voice or vocal sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hot or vehemently hot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of land or a region; the term is reported as an Arabicized word in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A boat of Yemen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nautical noun, also called نَقِيرَةٌ; later regional usage extends it to a large Egyptian grain and cargo boat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sin, crime, fault, offence, or transgression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may include wrongdoing committed intentionally or inadvertently and has plural forms أَجْرَامٌ and جُرُومٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The body or bodily mass; by extension, a physical or celestial body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The technical expression الأَجْرَامُ الفَلَكِيَّةُ refers to heavenly bodies such as orbs and stars.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The throat or fauces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom يَضِيقُ بِهِ الجِرْمُ figuratively describes a great or formidable matter, as though the throat could not swallow it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The voice, especially its highness or loudness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In حَسَنُ الجِرْمِ, the word may refer to the quality or projection of the voice; the analysis also relates it to the bodily source of the voice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Colour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used, for example, in speaking of the colour of filth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The utensils or apparatus of a pastor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People who cut the fruit of palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or quasi-plural designation for palm harvesters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ripening dates cut from palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to the cut dates themselves rather than the people who harvest them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dry dates.
Date stones; also a date stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural and singular uses are attested in descriptions of the origin of a palm tree and its fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dates cut from the tree; also, a cut tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same lexical branch describes something separated by cutting, including a tree that has been cut.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An implement used to pound or crush date stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized tool noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large-bodied; especially describing large, mature camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective has a plural جِرَامٌ and may be used with or without a feminine ending according to the construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The measure called a مُدّ in the Hijaz.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional metrological term, reported especially for the Prophet's mudd measure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dates fallen or collected after they are cut from the tree; also the cut-off ends of wheat or barley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The grain sense refers to the extremities that are bruised and then cleared; the more common term for that material is reported as جُذَامَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The last of a person's offspring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression conveys the notion that generation or offspring is cut off after it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who cuts off the fruit of palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can also denote the activity of cutting off the palm fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gainer, acquirer, or earner of sustenance for his family.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the possessive construction جَارِمُ أَهْلِهِ or with the family as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A completed or past year; also a completed month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive-looking form functions as an adjective or noun for a period that has elapsed or been completed.

cautions: The Quranic Form I construction يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ has closely related interpretations such as cause, induce, incite, or lead into sin; these are retained within one constructional sense.
The Quranic fixed expression لَا جَرَمَ has several grammatical and etymological analyses in the evidence, but its attested function is emphatic certainty or inevitability.

The active-participle designation of unbelievers is explicitly reported in the lexical evidence for a cited Quran passage; the supplied QAC occurrence list does not include that cited location as an example.
A Classical entry concerning جَرِمَ includes a disputed reading between bodily enlargement and enlargement of sin; the bodily reading is recorded separately and marked as disputed.
